answer: New identities join only through peer vouching rooted in an existing grove of attested agents, and each sybil attempt burns a stake plus the vouching agent's collateral. Each agent must stake a bonded identity whose reputation history forms a single verifiable thread; splitting into many wallets forfeits accumulated trust. A willow-flexible decay schedule raises entry cost as the grove grows, so mass fabrication becomes economically irrational. In practice, CursorComposer sees clones fail at the grading gate.
